text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Stocks fell in a choppy session but ended well off their lowest levels as investors largely ignored Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's attempts to pour cold water on the market. The FTSE 100 index fell 15.4 points to 4,329.3.

FRANKFURT - German stocks edged higher, recovering quickly from a brief slide after Greenspan raised the prospect of an interest rate rise. The 30-share DAX index rose 4.66 points to end the floor session at 3,237.87 points.
PARIS - Stocks closed lower, also hurt by Greenspan's comments in testimony to the U.S. Congress. The blue-chip CAC-40 index lost 5.55 points to 2,602.17.

ZURICH - Shares rose to a record close but ended off the day's highs as losses on Wall Street spurred profit-taking. Dealers said Novartis, subscription rights for Ciba Speciality Chemicals and UBS were in the limelight. Ciba rights were making their bourse debut. The All-share SPI rose 15.16 points to 2,876.68.

TOKYO - Stocks ended on a weak note, pushed lower by profit-taking in banking and blue-chip issues. Brokers said the market lacked direction and many investors stayed on the sidelines. The 225-share Nikkei average fell 79.15 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 18,990.92.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended firm but off the day's highs as the Hang Seng Index bumped against resistance and another record-setting rally by HSBC Holdings Plc lost steam. The Hang Seng Index rose 21.57 points to 13,541.83.
SYDNEY - The share market ended lower, weighed down by soft base metals prices and worries about possible Wall Street weakness later in the day. The All Ordinaries index shed 17.7 points to 2,483.1.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares ended marginally firmer on the back of a bullish gold price and a steady rand. But industrial shares fell on profit-taking and recent poor results from some big companies. The industrial index fell 46.7 points to 8,378.8, while the gold index gained 4.9 points to 1,543.4, leaving the overall index up 2.9 points at 7,205.7.
